messages:
Marco: heads-up — ams GPU fleet showing a sustained eviction surge and token latency climbing. traces point to ~20% of jobs hitting GPU memory reclaim. no customer-facing errors yet but 95th latency +200ms.
Anya: on it. I see a network retransmit increase on the ams-1 fabric and several pods retransmitting large KV cache prefixes. could be amplified by a recent batching change.
Sanjeev: can we start a soft traffic shift to euc1 and iad while we triage? weighted shift rather than full failover to avoid overload.
Marco: yes — suggested weights: ams 60 -> 30, euc1 30 -> 50, iad 10 -> 20 for next 10m. will run dry-run first.
Jess: note for runbook: we should have a quick checklist for "soft shift" vs "hard failover". current playbook only mentions full region failover.
Anya: doing dry-run now. quick command I used to validate routing policy: `curl -X POST https://routing-api/reweight -d '{"from":"ams","to":["euc1","iad"],"weights":[30,20]}'`
Sanjeev: watching metrics — evictions start to fall after the first minute of shift. 95th latency stabilizing. good sign.
Marco: OpsBot created incident INC-2026-413 and pinned logs. OpsBot: Incident INC-2026-413 opened by Marco. Related runbooks: infra/failover, infra/warm-pool.
Anya: root cause hypothesis: a recent change to per-tenant batching increased prefix persistency which combined with brief network retransmits caused KV cache thrash and downstream memory pressure on GPUs.
Jess: action item: add a new troubleshooting step in the runbook to check `kv-cache hit_ratio` and `batch-size` deltas before escalating to failover.
Sanjeev: also recommend a safety threshold edit: if GPU eviction_rate >= 10% for 5m AND 95th token latency +150ms, auto-trigger soft-shift (as Marco ran). currently we only have manual guidance.
Marco: agreed. add automation to alert owners and open a coordinated shift proposal in the routing queue.
Anya: notes for ops checklist (to add to runbook):
- verify warm-pool capacity available in target regions
- validate KMS and model access on warm nodes
- dry-run routing weights with `--simulate` flag
- watch eviction_rate / gpu_mem_pressure / net_retransmits
- if metrics improve within 3m, slowly ramp back to original weights over 10m

Sample commands to include in runbook:
```
# simulate weighted shift
curl -X POST https://routing-api/reweight -d '{"from":"ams","to":["euc1","iad"],"weights":[30,20],"simulate":true}'

# real shift (example)
curl -X POST https://routing-api/reweight -d '{"from":"ams","to":["euc1","iad"],"weights":[30,20]}'

# drain a problematic node (only if we need to take nodes out)
kubectl drain gpu-node-42 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=60
```
Jess: post-incident edits (assigned):
- infra/failover: add "soft-shift" procedure and simulation commands
- infra/thresholds: add eviction_rate and latency compound rule
- infra/triage: add kv-cache and batch-size quick checks

Sanjeev: cost note — soft-shift to other regions increases egress and inter-region model loads. we should add a cost guard: if predicted cross-region spend > $X/hour, require oncall approval to continue beyond 30m.
Marco: agreed — add a numeric placeholder and we can tune after next billing run.
Anya: follow-up tasks for this thread:
- (Anya) create PR with runbook edits and checklist
- (Jess) add threshold rule and automation ticket for soft-shift triggers
- (Sanjeev) modelling of cost impact for 30/60/120 minute sustained shifts
- (Marco) add example run commands to infra repo and link in runbook

Sanjeev: thanks all. I'm keeping monitoring open for 45m. if we re-hit >12% evictions then we escalate to full region failover.
Marco: closing loop — 30min post-shift numbers look stable. leaving incident open for runbook PRs. :thumbsup:
